collection.description: An elder thinks about the little things they never got round to: do one of them today, or let some stay undone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been thinking about the little things (subject.he/she) never got round to. Not the big ones. Small ones. (subject.He/She) has never climbed to the very top of the big rock at the end of the beach. (subject.He/She) has never tasted the sour red berries the children dare each other to eat. (subject.He/She) has never once slept outside under the stars, all night. There was always a reason not to.

choices.label: Decide Some Things Can Stay Undone

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) thinks about it all afternoon. Some of the things (subject.he/she) never did, (subject.he/she) would still like to do. Some, (subject.he/she) realizes, (subject.he/she) never actually wanted to: (subject.he/she) just thought (subject.he/she) should. (subject.He/She) doesn't feel like (subject.he/she) has missed out, exactly. (subject.He/She) feels like (subject.he/she) has lived a different list. That night, though, (subject.he/she) does take a blanket outside, just to see.

a__fx.name: Answer A
a__fx.text: (subject) eats a sour red berry. It is exactly as sour as the children say. (subject.His/Her) whole face folds up. (child), a watching child, laughs so hard (child.he/she) falls over. (subject) laughs too, eyes streaming. "Well," (subject.he/she) says, when (subject.he/she) can speak, "I'm glad I didn't do THAT one sooner." (subject.He/She) crosses it off. The rock can wait for tomorrow.
